*.text: Kansas context. The Kansas Corporation Commission (KCC) regulates the utilities and its docket numbers look like 25-EKCE-207-RTS. Air construction permits come from the Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) Bureau of Air, and the state permit system is KEIMS at keims.kdhe.ks.gov, which is script-driven but not closed. A harvested permit index may exist under work/permits/us-ks/ for your plant; read it first. Almost all of Kansas is in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP). Evergy Kansas Central is the former Westar and Evergy Kansas South is the former Kansas Gas and Electric.

L100001043000.text: Viola Generating Station, Sumner County, about 705 to 710 MW combined cycle owned half by Evergy Kansas Central and half by Evergy Missouri West. The KCC approved cost recovery in July 2025 and Evergy's first quarter 2026 report says the water main was under way and the baseline schedule was being set. The EIA file for August 2026 lists generator VIO1 at 765 MW with regulatory approvals received. GEM says 765 MW and start year 2029. Check the nameplate against the air permit or the KCC filings, whether construction has begun, and the start year. The brief's location task applies too.

L100001023601.text: McNew Generating Station, Reno County next to South Hutchinson, about 705 to 710 MW combined cycle owned half by Evergy Kansas Central and half by Evergy Missouri West. Evergy's first quarter 2026 report (May 8, 2026) says it is being built under a Kiewit engineering contract with Mitsubishi supplying the power equipment, and a generator tie line siting application was filed with the KCC on November 14, 2025 (docket 26-EKCE-0148-STG). In service is expected in January 2030. If construction has started, the status should say so with a dated source. The plant's location accuracy is approximate, so run the location ladder; the EIA table gives an address of TBD in Hutchison.

L100001023564.text: Walnut Energy Center power station is a 54.9 MW pre-construction unit owned by the Kansas Power Pool at Winfield. The ID matcher found EIA plant 7013 (East 12th Street, Cowley County) at the same point, with a 26.5 MW gas steam unit and a 1.6 MW backup unit. Say in a question whether that is this plant and give the plant code and generator IDs. Then find out whether the new engine has been built, from the Winfield city commission minutes, the Kansas Power Pool, or an air permit. GEM's start year and technology should follow the documents.

L100001063349.text: This plant is an unsited placeholder for capacity in Evergy Kansas Central's May 2025 plan update. It has no real site, and its map point was never set from a document. Do not run the location ladder on it, do not fill City, and do not stage coordinates. Skip the location and City tasks above and say in one plain sentence in your notes that the plant has no site. Answer the dated status history question from the plan or the backlog sheet's note if either gives a date. Check whether this block duplicates Viola or McNew, which together are the 355 MW blocks of 2029 and 2030 in the plan, and raise a question if it does.
